item.title: Version 1.2.25 (Build 20260916)
item.description:
What's New

fix(engine): drop the cancelled 'd' modifier when "ddd" undoes "đ"

Typing d-d-d-o-s shows "ddó" on screen, but restore-on-wrong-spelling replayed

"dddos" instead of "ddos". The third 'd' was counted twice in the restore record:

insertD's undo branch stripped TONE_MASK without removing the modifier keystroke

that dd→đ had recorded, while the vRestore branch of processKey re-inserts that

same key as its own entry.

The undo branch now drops it through a new TypingBuffer.removeModifier(at:keyCode:),

which targets the key the undo actually cancelled rather than the newest modifier —

an entry can carry both a horn and a tone.

This stays scoped to 'd'. The other undo gestures must keep the cancelled modifier:

a tone key never reaches the screen, so the record is what heals the swallowed

keystroke ("address" restores both 's'), and a vowel undo leaves Vietnamese off for

the rest of the word, so no restore ever runs. Only the 'd' path re-enables

processing (the "Allow d after consonant" rule in insertKey), which is what exposed

the double count.

Also bump CURRENTPROJECTVERSION to 20260916.
